"Revisiting Europe's temperate forests: Palaeoecological evidence for an herbivory-driven woodland-grassland mosaic biome". Biological Conservation. 316: 111749. doi:10.1016/j.biocon.2026.111749
payload.description_html:
From source: Artistic palaeo-reconstructions of ecosystem states in Central Europe over the last 23 million years, focusing on large herbivores and taxa indicative of openness. First row Neogene – evolutionary origin of present taxa, second row Pleistocene – pre-Homo sapiens baseline, third row Holocene – non-analogous ecosystems shaped by Homo sapiens.
  • A) Early Late Miocene (Vallesian - ~10 Mya) – present are Gleditsia (with trunk spines protecting against debarking), Torreya (highly poisonous yew relative), Sequoia abietina, Taxodium/Glyptostrobus, Pinus, Quercus drymeja, Carpinus grandis, Alnus, Osmunda (Kovar-Eder and Schweigert, 2018; Kunzmann et al., 2022; Worobiec et al., 2021), forb-rich herb layer (Feurdean and Vasiliev, 2019) with open habitat plants Armeria, Artemisia, Linum, Plantago, Potentilla (Łańcucka-Środoniowa, 1963), Sanguisorba (Denk et al., 2018), cf. Sagina (Geier et al., 2022) (with a present representatives reliant on disturbed soil), ground squirrel Spermophilinus bredai (Franzen et al., 2013), open habitat birds: kestrel (Falco tinnunculus atavus), bustard (Otis), little owl (Athene noctua veta), lark (Aulauda); and herbivores: proboscideans (Gomphotherium anguistidens and Zygolophodon turicensis), chalicothere (Chalicotherium goldfussi), rhinoceros (Aceratherium incisivum), swine (Parachleuastochoerus kretzoii) (Eastham et al., 2016), a group of early horses (Hipparion), and a river dam made by early wood-cutting beavers (Castor) (Plint et al., 2020).
Paintings by Márton Zsoldos. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)
